Lessons.Title: How Many Solutions?
ExplanationParagraphs: Learning goal: relate solutions of f(x)=0 to x-intercepts of graphs and classify when a quadratic equation has zero, one or two DISTINCT real solutions. First-party Edulytiks adaptation of Illustrative Mathematics Algebra 1 First Edition Unit 7 Lesson 5 teacher https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/teachers/1/7/5/preparation.html and student https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/students/1/7/5/index.html (CC BY 4.0). Source includes graph-based investigations and algebraic re-expression.

Three original functions: A(x)=(x−2)²+1 has minimum1 and no x-intercepts, so A(x)=0 has no real roots. B(x)=(x−2)² touches axis at x2, so one distinct root. C(x)=(x−2)²−9 crosses at x=−1 and x5, so two roots. All share symmetry axis x2; moving constant changes the number of intersections.

At target output y=0, a parabola can miss, touch, or cross the horizontal axis twice. Two algebraic repeated factors such as (x−2)(x−2)=0 do not mean two distinct numerical answers. For equations in standard form the discriminant can later provide this count without graphing, but it is not necessary for this exploratory source lesson.

Student task: draw three graphs with aligned axes, classify each using vertex relative to y0, explain algebraic checks and critique someone listing root2 twice. Teacher-scored rubric0–2 each for accurate graphs, correct distinct solution count, algebra/graph connection and explanation of tangency.

KeyConcepts.Title: No real roots
KeyConcepts.Definition: An upward parabola whose minimum is above zero does not meet x-axis.

KeyConcepts.Title: One distinct root
KeyConcepts.Definition: A parabola tangent to x-axis touches at its vertex.

KeyConcepts.Title: Two distinct roots
KeyConcepts.Definition: A parabola cutting the axis in two points has two real solutions.

WorkedExamples.Title: Classify graph above zero
WorkedExamples.Question: Solve(x−2)²+1=0.
WorkedExamples.Method: Solve the original independently authored equation and check every candidate in the source expression.
Steps: It cannot equal zero for real x.

WorkedExamples.Title: Find single tangent root
WorkedExamples.Question: Solve(x−2)²=0.
WorkedExamples.Method: Solve the original independently authored equation and check every candidate in the source expression.
Steps: Square equals zero only if base is zero.
WorkedExamples.Check: Root repeated algebraically, not two distinct x-values.

WorkedExamples.Title: Find two crossing roots
WorkedExamples.Question: Solve(x−2)²−9=0.
WorkedExamples.Method: Solve the original independently authored equation and check every candidate in the source expression.

CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Double root is one numerical input.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Assuming all quadratics cross horizontal axis
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Vertex can remain entirely above/below axis.

SummaryPoints: A parabola may have none, one tangent root or two distinct roots.
Original A,B,C demonstrate all three cases.
Teacher scores graph and algebraic explanation.
